# Netanyahu predicts Iran’s fall, top general warns of new war

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu (middle) attends a ceremony marking the third anniversary of the October 7 attack on October 5, 2026.



Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu predicted the eventual fall of Iran’s leadership while the Islamic Republic’s top armed forces commander warned a new conflict would engulf the region, sharpening exchanges over the prospect of renewed fighting on Monday.

The warnings came during a day that also saw Iran execute two protesters detained during the January uprising, the Revolutionary Guards threaten a tanker in the Strait of Hormuz, and Yemeni government forces launch a major offensive against the Iran-backed Houthis.

**Netanyahu says Iran is fighting for survival**

Iran’s leadership is weaker than at any point since its establishment and is fighting for survival, Netanyahu said at a ceremony marking the third anniversary of the October 7 attack.

“The tyranny is weaker than it has ever been since its establishment. It is fighting for its life, and its end is to disappear — or rather, to pass from the world,” Netanyahu said.

Netanyahu portrayed the October 7 attack as the opening stage of an Iranian-led effort to destroy Israel. He described what he called a three-pronged Iranian strategy involving armed groups surrounding Israel, thousands of missiles aimed at the country and nuclear weapons intended to destroy it.

# Saudi-backed forces say they retook key Red Sea port in anti-Houthi offensive

Members of Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces riding on a military pickup truck in Taiz province, Yemen.



Saudi-backed Yemeni forces said Monday they had retaken Mokha and advanced around the strategic Bab al-Mandeb Strait, one day after launching a major offensive to recover territory seized by the Iran-backed Houthis last month.

The armed forces of Yemen’s internationally recognized government said they had recaptured the port, which the Houthis seized last month, Reuters reported. Military spokesman Majed al-Nuzaili also reported the capture of Dhubab airport and the cutting of the road linking Dhubab to Mokha.

Saudi-led coalition spokesperson Maj. Gen. Turki al-Malki said 100 fighter jets were participating in Operation Yemen Dawn, providing round-the-clock support for ground forces and air cover over Bab al-Mandeb. He said the campaign had destroyed 324 “high-value” Houthi targets.

The Houthis earlier denied reports of government advances around the strait.

Yemen’s Information Minister Moammar al-Eryani told Reuters government forces had secured effective control of Bab al-Mandeb, although another government source said fighting continued at a nearby military base.

events.content_detail:
The chief executive of Saudi Aramco said Monday it could take up to two years to rebuild global oil inventories, warning that the squeeze on supplies could yet get worse as the U.S.-Iran war drags on.

Speaking at the Energy Intelligence conference in London, Saudi Aramco CEO Amin Nasser said pressure at both ends of the barrel will intensify until the strategically vital Strait of Hormuz fully reopens and confidence returns to energy markets.

The war has severely disrupted shipping through the strait, a narrow waterway that typically handles around 20% of the world's oil and liquefied natural gas supplies, sending shock waves through the global economy.

"Even then, replenishing inventories while meeting demand could take up to two years," Nasser said, according to Reuters.

His comments come shortly after G7 governments agreed on Friday to release 100 million barrels of diesel and crude from emergency reserves, following pressure from U.S. President Donald Trump.

The G7 members are France, Canada, Germany, Italy, Japan, the United Kingdom and the U.S. France currently holds the group's presidency. The European Union also participates in its meetings.

Aramco's Nasser said nearly 3 billion barrels of oil supply had been lost since the U.S. and Israel launched military strikes on Iran in late February, while 1 billion barrels of oil had been released from stocks.

# Russian strikes on Black Sea ports could cost Ukraine at least $8 billion

[Business](https://english.nv.ua/amp/business.html)

5 October, 02:49 PM

Russian strikes on Black Sea ports have effectively paralyzed Ukraine’s main grain export route, potentially costing the country at least $8 billion in revenue by summer 2027, [the Financial Times reported](https://www.ft.com/content/cc96ac01-7929-4954-97a3-7b30e00ef324?syn-25a6b1a6=1) on Oct. 5.

Such losses would amount to about 20% of Ukraine’s total export revenue last year. The figure is a projection based on a prolonged shutdown of port operations, not losses that have already been recorded.

Ukraine had planned to export 64 million metric tons of agricultural products this year. However, without the resumption of maritime shipping, the country would be able to export no more than half that amount, according to Vysotskyi.

# Greg Lui Chip Smuggling Scheme Possibly Linked to Supermicro Indictment

A review of Malaysian and U.S. public records points to the entities involved in an alleged scheme to smuggle hundreds of millions of dollars worth of AI servers to China

![AFP VW G v HighRes ChinaEconomy](https://dominotheory.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/AFP-VW-G-v-HighRes-ChinaEconomy--1280x720.jpg) NVIDIA’s logo displayed at a booth during a China supply chain trade show in Beijing in July 2025. (Photo: Jade Gao/AFP)

Federal authorities have arrested California businessman Greg Lui and indicted him with conspiracy to smuggle more than $300 million worth of controlled AI servers to China.

The scheme, detailed in an [indictment](https://www.justice.gov/usao-cdca/pr/san-gabriel-man-arrested-federal-charges-alleging-he-smuggled-china-more-300-million) document published on Thursday, involved shipping AI servers to Malaysia and Singapore, where the Lui falsely represented those countries as the servers’ final destinations.

Lui’s company, Earthmade, received more than $176 million from Malaysian transhipment companies between January and October of 2024.
